title: Sur Empire
capsule: The Sur Empire was an Afghan Pashtun dynasty founded by Sher Shah Suri, who defeated the Mughal emperor Humayun at Chausa (1539) and Kanauj (1540) and drove him into Persian exile. At its peak under Sher Shah (r. 1540–1545), the empire controlled most of northern India from Bengal to Punjab; Sher Shah reformed coinage, built the Grand Trunk Road, and reorganized provincial administration. His death in a gunpowder accident at Kalinjar (1545) set off succession struggles, and Humayun retook Delhi in 1555, ending effective Sur power; the last Sur claimant, Sikandar Shah Suri, was defeated at Sirhind that same year. Our dataset attests the empire through 1594, reflecting residual Sur-aligned resistance in Bengal and Orissa after the main dynasty's fall.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The empire's core territory in the Indo-Gangetic plain is well documented through Mughal and Sur administrative records and numismatic evidence; peripheral extents in Bengal and the western Deccan are reconstructed from chronicle sources and are less precisely bounded.
